heading.en: Why are there gaps in railway tracks?

hook.en: Look closely at old railway lines: small gaps are left between rails. On a hot afternoon the steel grows longer, and without the gaps the track would buckle.
hook.kn: ಹಳೆಯ ರೈಲು ಹಳಿಗಳ ನಡುವೆ ಸಣ್ಣ ಅಂತರ ಬಿಟ್ಟಿರುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಬಿಸಿ ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನ ಉಕ್ಕು ಉದ್ದವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ; ಅಂತರವಿಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ಹಳಿ ಬಾಗುತ್ತಿತ್ತು.

title.en: Use the coefficients of linear, area and volume expansion
Explain the anomalous expansion of water

say.en: Look closely at old railway lines: small gaps are left between rails. On a hot afternoon the steel grows longer, and without the gaps the track would buckle. In this lesson: Use the coefficients of linear, area and volume expansion.
Explain the anomalous expansion of water.

body.en: Most substances expand on heating. For a small rise ΔT, ΔL/L = α_l ΔT, ΔA/A = α_A ΔT and ΔV/V = α_V ΔT. For an isotropic solid α_A = 2α_l and α_V = 3α_l. Metals have α_l of the order of 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹. If a rod is clamped so it cannot expand, a *thermal* stress YαΔT develops.
body.kn: ಬಿಸಿ ಮಾಡಿದಾಗ ವಸ್ತುಗಳು ವ್ಯಾಕೋಚಿಸುತ್ತವೆ: ΔL/L = α_l ΔT, ΔV/V = α_V ΔT. ಸಮದಿಶೀಯ ಘನಕ್ಕೆ α_A = 2α_l, α_V = 3α_l. ಹಿಡಿದಿಟ್ಟ ಸರಳಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಉಷ್ಣ ಪ್ರತಿಬಲ YαΔT ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Most substances expand on heating. For a small rise delta T, delta L over L equals alpha _l delta T, delta A over A equals alpha _A delta T and delta V over V equals alpha _V delta T. For an isotropic solid alpha _A equals 2 alpha _l and alpha _V equals 3 alpha _l. Metals have alpha _l of the order of 10 to the power minus 5 kelvin to the power minus 1. If a rod is clamped so it cannot expand, a thermal stress Y alpha delta T develops. alpha _l: alpha _A: alpha _V equals 1: 2: 3.
say.kn: ಬಿಸಿ ಮಾಡಿದಾಗ ವಸ್ತುಗಳು ವ್ಯಾಕೋಚಿಸುತ್ತವೆ: delta L over L equals alpha _l delta T, delta V over V equals alpha _V delta T. ಸಮದಿಶೀಯ ಘನಕ್ಕೆ alpha _A equals 2 alpha _l, alpha _V equals 3 alpha _l. ಹಿಡಿದಿಟ್ಟ ಸರಳಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಉಷ್ಣ ಪ್ರತಿಬಲ Y alpha delta T ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Thermal stress equals Y alpha delta T.
A rod of length L is heated through ΔT. It grows by ΔL, proportional to both L and ΔT.
A square plate of side L becomes L plus ΔL. Its area grows by about 2 alpha L squared ΔT, so the area coefficient is twice alpha. For volume, it is three times.
A 10 metre steel rail, alpha 1.2 times ten to the minus 5, warms by 40 kelvin. It grows by 4.8 millimetres, so gaps are left between rails.
Clamp the rod so it cannot expand. The walls must compress it back by the same strain, which needs a stress Y alpha ΔT, about 96 megapascal for steel.
Water is odd: from 0 to 4 degrees Celsius it contracts. It is densest at 4 degrees, so lakes freeze from the top and fish survive below.

body.en: *Water* contracts when heated from 0 °C to 4 °C, so it is densest at 4 °C. In winter the top of a lake cools and sinks until the whole lake is at 4 °C; then the surface freezes first while water below stays at about 4 °C, and fish survive.

tagline.en: Temperature scales and conversions, linear, area and volume expansion, and the anomalous expansion of water.

say.en: Worked example. On a 45 °C afternoon in Delhi: $t_F = \tfrac95(45) + 32 = 81 + 32 = 113$ °F, and $T = 45 + 273.15 = 318.15$ K.

Worked example. A 12 m steel rail ($\alpha = 1.2\times10^{-5}$ K⁻¹) warms by 40 K from a winter night to a summer afternoon. $\Delta L = 1.2\times10^{-5}\times12\times40 = 5.76\times10^{-3}$ m $\approx 5.8$ mm.

Water contracts when heated from 0 °C to 4 °C and expands only above 4 °C, so it is densest at 4 °C. In a cold lake the 4 °C water sinks, ice forms on top and insulates the water below, and fish survive the winter.

problem.en: A steel rail is 10 m long at 20 °C. How much longer is it at 60 °C? (α = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹)

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A steel rail is 10 m long at 20 °C. How much longer is it at 60 °C? (α = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹)

say.en: Let us solve this together. A steel rail is 10 metres long at 20 degrees Celsius. How much longer is it at 60 degrees Celsius? (alpha equals 1.2 times 10 to the power minus 5 kelvin to the power minus 1).
delta T equals 60 minus 20 equals 40 kelvin.
delta L equals alpha Ldelta T equals 1.2 times 10 to the power minus 5 times 10 times 40 equals 4.8 times 10 to the power minus 3 metres.
So the answer is 4.8 millimetres.

body.en: Linear, area and volume expansion coefficients of an isotropic solid are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 — one for each dimension that grows.
